title: Cylinder 10 Glow Plug Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 10. Glow plugs heat the cylinders so a diesel engine starts easily in cold weather.
symptoms: Rough running or white smoke right after a cold start

causes.name: Damaged glow plug wire or connector

checks: Measure the cylinder 10 glow plug resistance
Inspect the glow plug wire and connector
fix: Usually a new glow plug; a wiring repair or control module if the plug tests good.

title: Glow Plug Control Module to PCM Communication Circuit
plain: The engine computer and the glow plug control module are having trouble communicating. Glow plugs heat the cylinders so a diesel engine starts easily in cold weather.
symptoms: Rough running or white smoke right after a cold start

causes.name: Damaged wiring or corroded connector between the computer and the module
Poor power or ground at the module

checks: Inspect the module connector and the wiring to the engine computer
Check module power and ground
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new glow plug control module.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the engine computer power relay. This part supplies main power to the engine computer and keeps it on briefly after shutdown.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Battery may drain overnight if the relay sticks on

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the engine computer power relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the engine computer power relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new engine computer power relay if it tests bad.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the engine computer power relay, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part supplies main power to the engine computer and keeps it on briefly after shutdown.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Battery may drain overnight if the relay sticks on
checks: Inspect the engine computer power relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the engine computer power relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new engine computer power relay if it tests bad.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the engine computer power relay, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part supplies main power to the engine computer and keeps it on briefly after shutdown.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Battery may drain overnight if the relay sticks on

causes.name: Faulty or shorted engine computer power relay

checks: Inspect the engine computer power relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the engine computer power relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new engine computer power relay if it tests bad.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit/Open
plain: The computer checks the voltage coming out of its own power relay, and that sense signal is missing.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Battery may drain overnight if the relay sticks on

causes.name: Blown fuse in the relay output circuit
Weak battery or poor battery connections

checks: Check the power relay and the fuses it feeds
Test the battery and clean the terminals
Inspect wiring at the fuse box and computer
fix: Usually a new power relay or fuse, or a wiring repair.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
plain: The computer checks the voltage coming out of its own power relay, and that sense signal is too low.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Battery may drain overnight if the relay sticks on

causes.name: Blown fuse in the relay output circuit
Weak battery or poor battery connections

checks: Check the power relay and the fuses it feeds
Test the battery and clean the terminals
Inspect wiring at the fuse box and computer
fix: Usually a new power relay or fuse, or a wiring repair.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Early
plain: The power to the engine computer was cut off before it finished its shutdown routine after the engine was turned off.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery terminals or relay connection
Battery disconnected while the computer was still powered
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check the battery terminals and relay connections
Look for a service bulletin or software update (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Often a battery connection repair or new relay; some vehicles need a software update.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Late
plain: The power relay to the engine computer stayed on longer than it should after the engine was turned off.

causes.name: Another module keeping the computer awake
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Listen or feel for the relay clicking off after shutdown
Check for battery drain with the car parked
fix: Usually a new power relay; sometimes a wiring repair or software update.

title: Fan 1 Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the cooling fan 1 relay or control circuit, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part switches an electric radiator cooling fan on and off.
symptoms: Engine may overheat in traffic or with the A/C on
Cooling fan runs all the time or never runs

causes.name: Faulty cooling fan 1 relay or control circuit

checks: Inspect the cooling fan 1 relay or control circuit wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the cooling fan 1 relay or control circuit with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a new fan relay, fan control module or wiring repair; sometimes the fan motor.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "C" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "C" has dropped out or is not reaching the sensors. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the shared 5-volt circuit (such as a throttle, pedal or pressure sensor)
Chafed or damaged wiring shorted to ground

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "C" Circuit Low
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "C" is being pulled too low, usually by a short to ground. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the shared 5-volt circuit (such as a throttle, pedal or pressure sensor)
Chafed or damaged wiring shorted to ground

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "C" Circuit High
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "C" is too high, usually from a short to another voltage source. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: 5-volt supply wire shorted to a higher voltage
Faulty sensor on the shared circuit
Corroded connector letting moisture bridge pins

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: Fuel Pump Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
plain: The fuel pump control module found a problem of its own and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light. The real fault is stored in the fuel pump module.
symptoms: Possible hard starting, stalling or loss of power

causes.name: Fault stored in the fuel pump control module
Corroded connector or wiring at the fuel pump module

checks: Read the codes stored in the fuel pump control module
Inspect the module connector and wiring for corrosion
fix: Read and repair the fault stored in the fuel pump control module.

title: Throttle Actuator Control Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit for the electronic throttle warning light on the dashboard.
symptoms: Electronic throttle warning light not working or stuck on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem between the computer and the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the throttle warning light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or instrument cluster repair.
